description: A *factoring* splits the variables of a planning task into a *center* and *leaves* for decoupled search. The fork factoring uses the *causal graph*, which has an arc from variable `u` to `v` when some operator reads or writes `u` and writes `v`. Every *sink component* of this graph (a strongly connected component that no arc leaves) becomes a leaf, if it has at most 2^16 states; all other variables form the center. Each leaf then depends only on the center, and no leaf affects the center, so all operators on a leaf are priced inside it. It suits tasks like logistics, where many packages depend on shared vehicles.

papers.title: Beating LM-Cut with h^max (Sometimes): Fork-Decoupled State Space Search
papers.venue: International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS)

papers.authors: Daniel Gnad, Valerie Poser, Jörg Hoffmann
papers.title: Beyond Forks: Finding and Ranking Star Factorings for Decoupled Search
